items.title: Lonnie Liston Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 9, 2021
items.q: Aretha Frank— that church, you grow up in it and the music is fantastic

ctx.x: So was there a spiritual thread throughout your life that stayed with you and when you became a leader what role did it play in the music you created?

That was it. Because you know people don’t realize the church is very important, you know, for us I guess as black people, because even with Trane, his father and grandfather was preachers. Aretha Frank— that church, you grow up in it and the music is fantastic and so what I did was, you know, I took that spirituality and all of a sudden I became aware of Eastern philosophy and different religions and I started studying them and then you find out, well wait a minute, all religions and all philosophies are…
Some of the things you did with Pharoah Sanders, the music would be going along sort of peaceful, and then something would happen.
